steps.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)

evidence: Directly changes LICM noConflictingReadWrites behavior using MemorySSA dominance.
Permits additional hoisting of memory-affecting instructions in the default scalar optimization area, plausibly exercising stale MemorySSA-use/update paths.
features: licm, memory-hoisting, memoryssa, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar, path:llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM change modifies MemorySSA-based hoist-safety checking in noConflictingReadWrites. When considering a hoist rather than a sink, LICM now skips candidate memory accesses already dominated by the instruction's MemoryDef (IMD), preventing those accesses from being treated as conflicting. The added and updated LICM tests show newly permitted hoisting of inaccessible-memory writes when no genuine conflict exists, while retaining cases where a read of the same inaccessible memory blocks hoisting.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA; LICMPass; LNICMPass; loop_alias; ne_loop_alias; fn_write_inaccessible_mem; fn_read_inaccessible_mem
Behavioral change: In LICM hoist-safety analysis, ignores a memory access when the candidate instruction's MemoryDef dominates that access and the operation is a hoist rather than a sink.; Allows additional LICM hoisting when dominated MemorySSA accesses cannot represent an ordering conflict for the proposed hoist.; Changes tested LICM output by hoisting an inaccessible-memory-writing call out of a loop in non-conflicting cases.; Retains MemorySSA analysis preservation after successful LICM and loop-nest LICM transformations in the visible pass context.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; memory access
Reproducer link: The new tests exercise loop hoisting of calls with inaccessible-memory effects and mixed read/write memory behavior, which is a memory-transform scenario under optimization.; The issue reproduces at -O3 while MemorySSA is updated; LICM is an -O3 loop transformation capable of moving memory-affecting instructions.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; loop-mssa
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate because it directly changes a MemorySSA query that determines whether LICM may move a memory-affecting instruction. Permitting additional hoists can exercise MemorySSA update paths differently, and an incorrect safety/update interaction could plausibly lead to stale uses when an access is removed. The retrieved hunks do not show a call to MemorySSA::removeFromLookups, a MemorySSA updater change, or the reported assertion itself, so the evidence supports a plausible subsystem-level causal path rather than a demonstrated direct cause.
Causal confidence: 0.66
Build risk: Changes LICM implementation logic in a MemorySSA-dependent safety check.; Adds a loop-mssa LICM regression test and updates existing LICM output checks, providing targeted testability for the changed hoisting behavior.; The affected condition depends on MemorySSA dominance and hoist-versus-sink mode, so regressions may be input- and pipeline-order-sensitive.

+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)' < %s -S | FileCheck %s

+;; It should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_args(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]

+  %val = call i32 @fn_args(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %load)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x

+;; It should NOT hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[VAL]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %val)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}

The added and updated LICM tests show newly permitted hoisting of inaccessible-memory writes when no genuine conflict exists, while retaining cases where a read of the same inaccessible memory blocks hoisting.
behavioral_change: In LICM hoist-safety analysis, ignores a memory access when the candidate instruction's MemoryDef dominates that access and the operation is a hoist rather than a sink.
Allows additional LICM hoisting when dominated MemorySSA accesses cannot represent an ordering conflict for the proposed hoist.
Changes tested LICM output by hoisting an inaccessible-memory-writing call out of a loop in non-conflicting cases.
Retains MemorySSA analysis preservation after successful LICM and loop-nest LICM transformations in the visible pass context.

assertion_or_trace: MemorySSA
memory access
reproducer: The new tests exercise loop hoisting of calls with inaccessible-memory effects and mixed read/write memory behavior, which is a memory-transform scenario under optimization.
The issue reproduces at -O3 while MemorySSA is updated; LICM is an -O3 loop transformation capable of moving memory-affecting instructions.
issue_link.explanation: This is the strongest candidate because it directly changes a MemorySSA query that determines whether LICM may move a memory-affecting instruction. Permitting additional hoists can exercise MemorySSA update paths differently, and an incorrect safety/update interaction could plausibly lead to stale uses when an access is removed. The retrieved hunks do not show a call to MemorySSA::removeFromLookups, a MemorySSA updater change, or the reported assertion itself, so the evidence supports a plausible subsystem-level causal path rather than a demonstrated direct cause.

build_risk: Changes LICM implementation logic in a MemorySSA-dependent safety check.
Adds a loop-mssa LICM regression test and updates existing LICM output checks, providing targeted testability for the changed hoisting behavior.
The affected condition depends on MemorySSA dominance and hoist-versus-sink mode, so regressions may be input- and pipeline-order-sensitive.

top_candidates.subject: Revert [LICM] Remove unnecessary check during store hoisting (#195606)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM revert reinstates a conservative MemorySSA-based legality check in store/call hoisting. In noConflictingReadWrites, non-sinking motion is now rejected when the instruction memory definition does not dominate an optimized MemorySSA use, addressing cases where a clobber query follows a loop backedge and an optimized use can refer to an access outside the loop. The accompanying tests require affected stores and inaccessible-memory calls to remain in the loop.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def; loop_alias; unrelated_read
Behavioral change: LICM now returns false for non-sinking hoisting when MSSA->dominates(IMD, MU) is false.; The new restriction prevents motion past potentially interfering loads when an optimized MemorySSA use points outside the loop.; Store/call hoisting becomes more conservative for loop-backedge and optimized-use cases.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; getClobbering; Optimized Uses
Reproducer link: The new LICM test covers a loop where a preceding load may access the store location on the first iteration, while its clobber is liveOnEntry because the backedge pointer does not alias.; The affected behavior is loop store/call hoisting rather than the supplied reduced C -O3 crash.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; Scalar optimizer; MemorySSA
Causal explanation: This commit directly changes an LICM decision based on MemorySSA optimized uses and explicitly documents an outside-the-loop clobber/use condition. Such motion can affect the MemorySSA graph that LICM must preserve. However, the change is a defensive revert that blocks a class of hoists; no retrieved hunk changes MemorySSA removal or updater logic, and no hunk mentions removeFromLookups or an access still having uses. It is therefore more plausibly a mitigation for an unsafe transformation than a direct source of the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.28
Build risk: Implementation change is localized to LICM legality checking and does not alter public headers in the retrieved hunks.; Regression coverage was added or updated in LICM store-hoisting, call-hoisting, and inaccessible-memory-call tests.; The test expectation changes intentionally reduce some hoisting opportunities, so optimization-result regressions are a primary validation concern.

+; The store should not be hoisted here, because the location is accessed by the
+; preceding load. However, the clobbering memory access for that load is
+; liveOnEntry, because the pointer on the backedge does not alias. As such,
+; only checking whether the clobbering access is outside the loop is
+; insufficient.
+define i8 @load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def(i1 %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i8 @load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[C:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ @g1, %[[ENTRY]] ], [ @g2, %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = load i8, ptr [[PHI]], align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i8 1, ptr @g1, align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[V]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i8 [[V_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ @g1, %entry ], [ @g2, %loop ]
+  %v = load i8, ptr %phi
+  store i8 1, ptr @g1
+  br i1 %c, label %loop, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret i8 %v
+}

Summary: This VPlan/LoopVectorize change optimizes induction-variable resume values together with other loop exit values. The retrieved evidence is limited to LoopVectorize test expectation updates: vector recurrence extraction values are reassigned between the ordinary recurrence extract and the extract used for the scalar-resume PHI, changing the checked lane offsets from minus-one to minus-two and vice versa for different vectorization/unroll configurations.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved patch updates ExpandIRInsts regression expectations to preserve function-entry-count and branch-weight profile metadata while expanding large floating-point conversion operations. The checks now expect !prof metadata on generated conditional branches and switches, and adjust expected control-flow destinations in signed and unsigned x86_fp80-to-i129 expansion tests.
Changed symbols: si129tox86_fp80; ui129tox86_fp80; x86_fp80toui129; x86_fp80tosi129; si129tofloatv2; ui129tofloatv2; sitofp_i16_f16
Behavioral change: Expanded large FP conversion control flow is expected to retain function_entry_count metadata.; Generated conditional branches and switches are expected to carry branch_weights profile metadata.; The expected destination for negative-exponent checks in x86_fp80-to-i129 conversion expansion changes from the saturation-check block to the exponent-size-check block.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved hunk references MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; No retrieved hunk references the diagnostic that a memory access still has uses; No retrieved hunk touches MemorySSA.cpp or MemorySSA headers
Reproducer link: The visible coverage is for ExpandIRInsts expansion of large FP conversions and profile metadata propagation.; It does not show a reduced C testcase, -O3 MemorySSA crash, or memory-access deletion scenario.
Pass or subsystem link: ExpandIRInsts; profile metadata propagation; large floating-point conversion expansion
Causal explanation: The patch affects generated CFG shape and profile metadata during large FP conversion expansion. Profile metadata can influence later optimization decisions, but the retrieved evidence does not show memory operations, MemorySSA users, or MemorySSA update/removal logic. Therefore only an indirect and weak connection to the reported MemorySSA assertion is supported.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Retrieved hunks are regression-test expectation and metadata-input updates only.; Tests cover x86 large-FP conversion expansion, including x86_fp80 and i129 conversion paths.; The visible changes are sensitive to generated CFG labels and profile-metadata attachment, but no production implementation or MemorySSA change is shown.

Summary: This SROA change threads SROAOptions into SROA construction and adds coverage for opt-in aggregate-to-vector canonicalization of homogeneous structs. The new tests establish that the default O3 pipeline delays struct-to-vector canonicalization until after memcpyopt, changing how allocas, memcpy/memset sequences, and aggregate stores are rewritten.
Changed symbols: SROAPass::run; selectPartitionType; store_only_fp_tail; foo_flat; move_then_swap
Behavioral change: SROAPass::run now constructs SROA with Options rather than only PreserveCFG, enabling configured SROA behavior to reach the implementation.; The added tests exercise the aggregate-to-vector SROA option and distinguish canonicalized vector partitions from non-canonical aggregate partitions.; The default O3 phase-ordering test requires struct-to-vector canonicalization to occur after memcpyopt, allowing memcpyopt to collapse certain memcpy-based swaps into load/memmove/store sequences.; selectPartitionType now logs the selected direct vector, common type, integer fallback, and byte-array fallback decisions; the visible hunks do not show a semantic selection-rule change beyond this instrumentation.

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e98c9074e4f8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -S -passes='default<O3>' %s | FileCheck %s
+
+%pair = type { i64, i64 }
+%quad = type { i64, i64, i64, i64 }
+
+declare void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr noalias writeonly captures(none), ptr noalias readonly captures(none), i64, i1 immarg)
+declare void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr writeonly captures(none), i8, i64, i1 immarg)
+
+; This test verifies that the default O3 pipeline canonicalizes struct allocas
+; to vectors only after memcpyopt has run. The input pattern is:
+;
+;   memcpy tmp, obj, 16
+;   memset obj + 16, 0, 16
+;
+;  ----- SWAP(other, tmp) -----
+;
+;   memcpy swap.tmp, tmp, 16
+;   memcpy tmp, other, 16
+;   memcpy other, swap.tmp, 16
+;
+; It swaps the first 16-bytes of other and tmp, but the first 16-bytes of tmp
+; are the same as the first 16-bytes of obj. This comes from real code from
+; DuckDB, where the swap function is inlined. If struct-to-vector canonicalization
+; runs before memcpyopt, swap.tmp gets promoted to an SSA value and we are stuck
+; saving tmp to swap.tmp. Delaying canonicalization until after memcpyopt lets
+; memcpyopt notice that tmp and obj share the same first 16-bytes, so swap.tmp
+; is no longer needed and the IR collapses to a single load/memmove/store.
+define void @move_then_swap(ptr %dst, ptr %src, ptr %other) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @move_then_swap(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr writeonly captures(none) initializes((0, 16)) [[DST:%.*]], ptr readonly captures(none) [[SRC:%.*]], ptr captures(none) [[OTHER:%.*]]) local_unnamed_addr #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD:%.*]] = load <2 x i64>, ptr [[OTHER]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    tail call void @llvm.memmove.p0.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[OTHER]], ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[SRC]], i64 16, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store <2 x i64> [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD]], ptr [[DST]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  %obj = alloca %quad, align 8
+  %swap.tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %obj, i64 16, i1 false)
+  %obj.tail = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %obj, i64 16
+  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj.tail, i8 0, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %other, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %other, ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

steps.subject: [LoopInterchange] Do not interchange guarded imperfect loop nests (#201504)

evidence: Prevents interchange of guarded imperfect loop nests to avoid a semantic nontermination bug.
It blocks a transformation rather than changing MemorySSA bookkeeping or memory-access lifetime handling.
features: conservative-transform-disable, guarded-loop-legality, loop-interchange, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested is tightened to reject guarded imperfect loop nests: if an outer-loop header can branch directly to its latch as well as into the inner loop, the loops are no longer considered tightly nested and cannot be interchanged. The change is documented as avoiding illegal execution of the inner loop on guarded-off outer iterations, including cases where the inner-loop exit would no longer terminate. Tests add a guarded-inner-loop regression and update expected LoopInterchange output for guarded LCSSA/preheader cases.
Changed symbols: LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested; lcssa_08; main
Behavioral change: Requires the outer-loop header to branch only into the inner loop for a loop pair to qualify as tightly nested.; Rejects interchange when the outer header can bypass the inner loop and reach the outer latch.; Prevents interchange from executing an inner loop on outer iterations where its guard is false.; Produces a NotTightlyNested missed-optimization result for the new guarded-inner-loop case.
Reproducer link: The added regression contains loads and stores in a guarded nested loop, but it targets nontermination/semantic correctness of loop interchange rather than an optimizer crash.; No retrieved evidence connects the reported -O3 crash or the specific MemorySSA still-has-uses failure to guarded imperfect loop nests.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopInterchange; Transforms/Scalar; loop CFG and memory-operation transformation
Causal explanation: Loop interchange can alter control flow and memory-operation placement, so it is generally adjacent to MemorySSA-sensitive optimization behavior. This specific patch is conservative and blocks a transformation before it occurs; it neither changes MemorySSA nor exposes an access-removal/update mechanism. The available evidence consequently indicates low likelihood that it directly causes the reported MemorySSA::removeFromLookups assertion, though it could prevent an unrelated faulty interchange scenario.
Causal confidence: 0.13
Build risk: Changes production loop-interchange structural-legality logic.; Adds a regression test checking a missed-optimization remark and updates LoopInterchange FileCheck expectations.; No MemorySSA implementation, invalidation, or access-lifetime changes are present in the retrieved hunks.

diff --git a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
index 28eef9c2790d..b2e3bbe516ed 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
@@ -827,3 +827,18 @@ bool LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested(Loop *OuterLoop, Loop *InnerLoop) {
-  // A perfectly nested loop will not have any branch in between the outer and
-  // inner block i.e. outer header will branch to either inner preheader and
-  // outerloop latch.
+  // In a perfectly nested loop the outer header branches only into the inner
+  // loop. If it can also reach the outer latch, it conditionally guards the
+  // inner loop (an imperfect nest), so the inner loop runs on only a subset of
+  // the outer iterations. Interchanging such a nest would run the inner loop on
+  // every outer iteration, including the guarded-off ones, which is illegal
+  // when the inner loop relies on the guard to terminate (e.g. an eq/ne exit
+  // whose trip count is degenerate once the guard is false). Reject by allowing
+  // the outer header to branch only into the inner loop.
+  //
+  // TODO: This is conservative. A guarded nest is still safe to interchange
+  // when the inner loop has a computable trip count that is empty exactly when
+  // the guard is false, e.g.:
+  //   for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
+  //     if (M > 0)                  // loop-invariant guard
+  //       for (j = 0; j < M; j++)   // empty when M <= 0
+  //         A[j][i] = ...;
+  // Interchanging is legal here because the inner loop runs zero times on the
+  // guarded-off iterations.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..681dca5bbcba
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes=loop-interchange \
+; RUN:     -loop-interchange-profitabilities=ignore \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-missed='loop-interchange' -disable-output \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-output=%t
+; RUN: FileCheck -input-file=%t %s
+
+; The middle loop %for.j guards the inner loop %for.k: %for.k runs only when
+; %i != 0 (the outer loop's IV), and its exit %k.next == %i is only well-defined
+; under that guard. Interchanging %for.j and %for.k would run %for.k on every
+; iteration and spin when %i == 0, so the pass must not interchange this nest.
+;
+; Pseudo code:
+;   for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)
+;     for (j = 0; j < 2; j++)
+;       if (i != 0)                  // guard on the outer IV
+;         for (k = 0; ; k++) {       // terminates only when i != 0
+;           y[j][i][k] = x[i][k][j] + w[i][k][j];
+;           if (k + 1 == i) break;
+;         }
+
+; CHECK:      --- !Missed
+; CHECK-NEXT: Pass:            loop-interchange
+; CHECK-NEXT: Name:            NotTightlyNested
+; CHECK-NEXT: Function:        main
+
+@x = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@w = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@y = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+
+define i32 @main() {
+entry:
+  br label %for.i
+
+for.i:
+  %i = phi i32 [ %i.next, %for.i.inc ], [ 0, %entry ]
+  %i.is.zero = icmp eq i32 %i, 0
+  %xbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @x, i32 %i
+  %wbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @w, i32 %i
+  %ybase = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr @y, i32 %i
+  br label %for.j
+
+for.j:
+  %j = phi i32 [ %j.next, %for.j.inc ], [ 0, %for.i ]
+  br i1 %i.is.zero, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k.ph
+
+for.k.ph:
+  %xp = getelementptr i32, ptr %xbase, i32 %j
+  %wp = getelementptr i32, ptr %wbase, i32 %j
+  %yp = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr %ybase, i32 %j
+  br label %for.k
+
+for.k:
+  %k = phi i32 [ 0, %for.k.ph ], [ %k.next, %for.k ]
+  %xk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %xp, i32 %k
+  %xv = load i32, ptr %xk, align 4
+  %wk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %wp, i32 %k
+  %wv = load i32, ptr %wk, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %xv, %wv
+  %yk = getelementptr i32, ptr %yp, i32 %k
+  store i32 %add, ptr %yk, align 4
+  %k.next = add i32 %k, 1
+  %k.done = icmp eq i32 %k.next, %i
+  br i1 %k.done, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k
+
+for.j.inc:
+  %j.next = add i32 %j, 1
+  %j.cmp = icmp eq i32 %j, 0
+  br i1 %j.cmp, label %for.j, label %for.i.inc
+
+for.i.inc:
+  %i.next = add i32 %i, 1
+  %i.done = icmp eq i32 %i.next, 3
+  br i1 %i.done, label %exit, label %for.i
+
+exit:
+  ret i32 0
+}

Summary: LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested is tightened to reject guarded imperfect loop nests: if an outer-loop header can branch directly to its latch as well as into the inner loop, the loops are no longer considered tightly nested and cannot be interchanged. The change is documented as avoiding illegal execution of the inner loop on guarded-off outer iterations, including cases where the inner-loop exit would no longer terminate. Tests add a guarded-inner-loop regression and update expected LoopInterchange output for guarded LCSSA/preheader cases.
Changed symbols: LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested; lcssa_08; main
Behavioral change: Requires the outer-loop header to branch only into the inner loop for a loop pair to qualify as tightly nested.; Rejects interchange when the outer header can bypass the inner loop and reach the outer latch.; Prevents interchange from executing an inner loop on outer iterations where its guard is false.; Produces a NotTightlyNested missed-optimization result for the new guarded-inner-loop case.
Reproducer link: The added regression contains loads and stores in a guarded nested loop, but it targets nontermination/semantic correctness of loop interchange rather than an optimizer crash.; No retrieved evidence connects the reported -O3 crash or the specific MemorySSA still-has-uses failure to guarded imperfect loop nests.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopInterchange; Transforms/Scalar; loop CFG and memory-operation transformation
Causal explanation: Loop interchange can alter control flow and memory-operation placement, so it is generally adjacent to MemorySSA-sensitive optimization behavior. This specific patch is conservative and blocks a transformation before it occurs; it neither changes MemorySSA nor exposes an access-removal/update mechanism. diff --git a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
index 28eef9c2790d..b2e3bbe516ed 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
@@ -827,3 +827,18 @@ bool LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested(Loop *OuterLoop, Loop *InnerLoop) {
-  // A perfectly nested loop will not have any branch in between the outer and
-  // inner block i.e. outer header will branch to either inner preheader and
-  // outerloop latch.
+  // In a perfectly nested loop the outer header branches only into the inner
+  // loop. If it can also reach the outer latch, it conditionally guards the
+  // inner loop (an imperfect nest), so the inner loop runs on only a subset of
+  // the outer iterations. Interchanging such a nest would run the inner loop on
+  // every outer iteration, including the guarded-off ones, which is illegal
+  // when the inner loop relies on the guard to terminate (e.g. an eq/ne exit
+  // whose trip count is degenerate once the guard is false). Reject by allowing
+  // the outer header to branch only into the inner loop.
+  //
+  // TODO: This is conservative. A guarded nest is still safe to interchange
+  // when the inner loop has a computable trip count that is empty exactly when
+  // the guard is false, e.g.:
+  //   for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
+  //     if (M > 0)                  // loop-invariant guard
+  //       for (j = 0; j < M; j++)   // empty when M <= 0
+  //         A[j][i] = ...;
+  // Interchanging is legal here because the inner loop runs zero times on the
+  // guarded-off iterations.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..681dca5bbcba
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes=loop-interchange \
+; RUN:     -loop-interchange-profitabilities=ignore \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-missed='loop-interchange' -disable-output \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-output=%t
+; RUN: FileCheck -input-file=%t %s
+
+; The middle loop %for.j guards the inner loop %for.k: %for.k runs only when
+; %i != 0 (the outer loop's IV), and its exit %k.next == %i is only well-defined
+; under that guard. Interchanging %for.j and %for.k would run %for.k on every
+; iteration and spin when %i == 0, so the pass must not interchange this nest.
+;
+; Pseudo code:
+;   for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)
+;     for (j = 0; j < 2; j++)
+;       if (i != 0)                  // guard on the outer IV
+;         for (k = 0; ; k++) {       // terminates only when i != 0
+;           y[j][i][k] = x[i][k][j] + w[i][k][j];
+;           if (k + 1 == i) break;
+;         }
+
+; CHECK:      --- !Missed
+; CHECK-NEXT: Pass:            loop-interchange
+; CHECK-NEXT: Name:            NotTightlyNested
+; CHECK-NEXT: Function:        main
+
+@x = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@w = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@y = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+
+define i32 @main() {
+entry:
+  br label %for.i
+
+for.i:
+  %i = phi i32 [ %i.next, %for.i.inc ], [ 0, %entry ]
+  %i.is.zero = icmp eq i32 %i, 0
+  %xbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @x, i32 %i
+  %wbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @w, i32 %i
+  %ybase = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr @y, i32 %i
+  br label %for.j
+
+for.j:
+  %j = phi i32 [ %j.next, %for.j.inc ], [ 0, %for.i ]
+  br i1 %i.is.zero, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k.ph
+
+for.k.ph:
+  %xp = getelementptr i32, ptr %xbase, i32 %j
+  %wp = getelementptr i32, ptr %wbase, i32 %j
+  %yp = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr %ybase, i32 %j
+  br label %for.k
+
+for.k:
+  %k = phi i32 [ 0, %for.k.ph ], [ %k.next, %for.k ]
+  %xk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %xp, i32 %k
+  %xv = load i32, ptr %xk, align 4
+  %wk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %wp, i32 %k
+  %wv = load i32, ptr %wk, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %xv, %wv
+  %yk = getelementptr i32, ptr %yp, i32 %k
+  store i32 %add, ptr %yk, align 4
+  %k.next = add i32 %k, 1
+  %k.done = icmp eq i32 %k.next, %i
+  br i1 %k.done, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k
+
+for.j.inc:
+  %j.next = add i32 %j, 1
+  %j.cmp = icmp eq i32 %j, 0
+  br i1 %j.cmp, label %for.j, label %for.i.inc
+
+for.i.inc:
+  %i.next = add i32 %i, 1
+  %i.done = icmp eq i32 %i.next, 3
+  br i1 %i.done, label %exit, label %for.i
+
+exit:
+  ret i32 0
+}

top_candidates.subject: [LSR] Keep ICmpZero comparisons in integer domain to avoid inttoptr casts (#201970)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This Loop Strength Reduction change keeps pointer-originated ICmpZero uses in ScalarEvolution's effective integer type. LSRInstance::Expand changes the selected operand type from pointer to integer for such uses, and LSRInstance::Rewrite correspondingly avoids converting the expanded integer back to the original pointer type. The resulting rewritten comparison is an integer icmp and avoids generating inttoptr casts, with tests covering ordinary loop lowering and an exception-handling case.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::Expand; LSRInstance::Rewrite; LSRUse::ICmpZero; LoopStrengthReduce
Behavioral change: For an ICmpZero use whose original operand type is a pointer, LSR selects ScalarEvolution's effective integer SCEV type during expansion.; LSR suppresses the normal conversion of the expanded integer value back to the pointer operand type for that ICmpZero case.; Pointer comparisons such as icmp eq ptr derived-pointer, null can become integer comparisons such as icmp eq i64 induction-value, 0, eliminating the intermediate inttoptr cast.
Assertion or trace link: No visible reference to MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; No visible reference to 'Trying to remove memory access that still has uses'; Visible diagnostics and tests concern ICmpZero lowering and inttoptr avoidance
Reproducer link: The added regression test verifies LSR produces one integer induction variable and integer comparisons without inttoptr casts.; Existing LSR tests are updated to expect integer comparisons, including pr27056's catchpad path.; No Clang -O3 MemorySSA crash reproducer is present in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce scalar transformation; ScalarEvolution type selection; Indirectly relevant optimizer pipeline code, but no direct MemorySSA or MemorySSAUpdater changes
Causal explanation: LSR rewrites loop IR and can run in optimization pipelines where MemorySSA is maintained, so a type-sensitive rewrite could indirectly affect downstream analysis or updater interactions. However, the visible change is narrowly restricted to comparison operands and cast suppression; it does not add, remove, move, or update memory accesses, nor does it invoke MemorySSA APIs. The evidence therefore supports only a weak indirect causal link.
Causal confidence: 0.16
Build risk: The rewrite introduces a special type-consistency exception for pointer-typed ICmpZero uses, so incorrect applicability could produce invalid or unexpected typed IR.; The new regression test is target-dependent because it relies on TTI reporting legal scaled addressing.; Tests cover integer-domain comparisons and removal of inttoptr casts, including an exception-handling case, but do not exercise MemorySSA verification or the reported assertion.

index 000000000000..0d6a374f8669
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-reduce -S %s | FileCheck %s
+;
+; Verify that LSR keeps ICmpZero comparisons in the integer domain when the
+; original operands are pointers, avoiding inttoptr casts entirely. The loop
+; has three pointer IVs sharing the same stride; LSR should produce a single
+; integer IV and compare it directly against the precomputed bound.
+; Target-dependent because TTI must report that scaled addressing is legal.
+
+target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+target datalayout = "e-m:e-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
+
+define void @test_no_inttoptr_casts(ptr %base1, ptr %base2, ptr %base3, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @test_no_inttoptr_casts(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = shl i64 [[N:%.*]], 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ], [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE1:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP1:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE2:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP2:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE3:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_EXIT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_EXIT]], label [[CHECK:%.*]], label [[BODY:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       check:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP3:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i1 true, i1 [[CMP3]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[SEL]], label [[BODY]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V1:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V2:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP1]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUM:%.*]] = add i64 [[V1]], [[V2]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SUM]], ptr [[SCEVGEP2]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %bound1 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base1, i64 %n
+  %bound2 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base2, i64 %n
+  %bound3 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base3, i64 %n
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %p1 = phi ptr [ %base1, %entry ], [ %p1.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p2 = phi ptr [ %base2, %entry ], [ %p2.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p3 = phi ptr [ %base3, %entry ], [ %p3.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %cmp.exit = icmp eq ptr %p2, %bound2
+  br i1 %cmp.exit, label %check, label %body
+
+check:
+  %cmp1 = icmp ne ptr %p1, %bound1
+  %cmp3 = icmp ne ptr %p3, %bound3
+  %sel = select i1 %cmp1, i1 true, i1 %cmp3
+  br i1 %sel, label %body, label %exit
+
+body:
+  %v1 = load i64, ptr %p1, align 8
+  %v2 = load i64, ptr %p2, align 8
+  %sum = add i64 %v1, %v2
+  store i64 %sum, ptr %p3, align 8
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+loop.latch:
+  %p1.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p1, i64 8
+  %p2.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p2, i64 8
+  %p3.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p3, i64 8
+  br label %loop
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

The retrieved changes are entirely in llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange and contain no loop-interchange implementation changes.

top_candidates.subject: [LoopInterchange] Identify unsafe instructions for interchange (#201402)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: LoopInterchangeLegality::canInterchangeLoops is changed from a call-specific safety screen to a general instruction safety screen. Loads, stores, and pseudo probes remain excluded from this particular check, while any other instruction that may have side effects or may read memory now rejects interchange and emits an UnsafeInst missed-optimization remark. The accompanying tests update expected output so loop nests containing invokes or atomic operations remain uninterchanged.
Changed symbols: LoopInterchangeLegality::canInterchangeLoops; invoke_may_rw; atomicrmw; cmpxchg
Behavioral change: Replaces the prior CallInst-only interchange restriction with a per-instruction legality check.; Rejects loop interchange for non-load/store/non-pseudoprobe instructions that may have side effects or may read memory.; Treats potential callee memory reads as unsafe even when the call itself has no direct side effects.; Emits an OptimizationRemarkMissed named UnsafeInst when this broader safety rule blocks interchange.
Reproducer link: The new tests cover invokes that may read or write memory and atomic memory operations, both of which are memory-sensitive loop-interchange cases.; No retrieved test reproduces a crash, a MemorySSA removal failure, or the reported -O3 reduced-C testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopInterchange; Transforms/Scalar; loop memory-dependence legality
Causal explanation: The commit operates in a scalar loop transformation that can otherwise rearrange memory-accessing instructions, so it is relevant to optimizer memory behavior. But the implementation change is a conservative legality restriction: it prevents interchange for more unsafe instructions rather than adding a MemorySSA update path. No retrieved code references MemorySSA, removeFromLookups, access deletion, or analysis invalidation. It could only be related if the issue depends on LoopInterchange transforming a now-rejected case, and the supplied evidence does not establish that.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Changes production legality logic in llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp.; Regression tests update expected non-interchanged CFGs for invoke and atomic cases.; No build configuration, API, or MemorySSA-specific test changes are visible.

+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-reduce -S %s | FileCheck %s
+;
+; Verify that LSR keeps ICmpZero comparisons in the integer domain when the
+; original operands are pointers, avoiding inttoptr casts entirely. The loop
+; has three pointer IVs sharing the same stride; LSR should produce a single
+; integer IV and compare it directly against the precomputed bound.
+; Target-dependent because TTI must report that scaled addressing is legal.
+
+target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+target datalayout = "e-m:e-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

+; CHECK-LABEL: @test_no_inttoptr_casts(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = shl i64 [[N:%.*]], 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ], [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE1:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP1:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE2:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]

Summary: The LoopStrengthReduce change special-cases pointer-typed ICmpZero uses so LSR expands and retains comparison operands in ScalarEvolution's effective integer type rather than converting the expanded integer induction value back to a pointer with inttoptr. Rewrite correspondingly avoids inserting a type conversion for that ICmpZero case. New and updated tests verify integer-domain compares and removal of inttoptr instructions.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::Expand; LSRInstance::Rewrite; LSRUse::ICmpZero; test_no_inttoptr_casts; b_copy_ctor; f; _Z15IntegerToStringjjR7Vector2
Behavioral change: For an LSR ICmpZero use whose original operand type is pointer, Expand changes the requested operand type to ScalarEvolution's effective SCEV type, producing an integer-domain value.; Rewrite suppresses the normal FullV-to-OpTy conversion for pointer-typed ICmpZero uses because both operands were expanded as integers.; Pointer equality/null-style comparisons selected by LSR can become integer comparisons, eliminating generated inttoptr casts while preserving pointer-based GEPs for actual address computation.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved code or test mentions MemorySSA::removeFromLookups, trying to remove a memory access that still has uses, or the reported assertion.
Reproducer link: The new test contains a loop with loads and a store through three pointer induction variables, but its stated purpose is to prevent inttoptr generation and it does not exercise or report an -O3 MemorySSA crash.; Updated regressions check that LSR emits icmp eq i64 for an induction value rather than converting it to ptr for comparison.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; ScalarEvolution; Transforms/Scalar
Causal explanation: This is a substantive scalar-loop IR rewrite affecting pointer induction variables, comparison types, and the shape of loops containing loads and stores. Such changed IR can indirectly affect later MemorySSA users at -O3. However, the shown implementation does not create, remove, replace, or update memory instructions or MemorySSA accesses; it changes casts and comparison operands. The evidence supports moderate subsystem relevance but not a direct mechanism for removeFromLookups retaining uses.

+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       exit:

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved changes are SLPVectorizer test-expectation updates documenting that scalar intrinsic-call packs are now emitted as vector intrinsic calls or vector-library calls. In particular, scalar ctlz and powi call sequences are expected to collapse into vector intrinsics, while partial sin and atan2 packs are expected to use shuffle-based packing/unpacking around v2 intrinsic calls.
Changed symbols: cltz_test; PR53887_v4f64; int_sin_4x; atan2_4x; int_atan2_4x; SLPVectorizer test checks
Behavioral change: Expected SLP output for scalar ctlz calls changes from extractelement/call/insertelement chains to a single llvm.ctlz.v2i8 call.; Expected SLP output for scalar powi calls changes to a llvm.powi.v4f64.i32 vector intrinsic call.; Expected partial sin and atan2 packs change from independent scalar calls and insertelement chains to shufflevector packing, v2 intrinsic calls, and shuffle-based result insertion.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved hunk mentions MemorySSA; No retrieved hunk mentions removeFromLookups; No retrieved hunk mentions a memory access with remaining uses
Reproducer link: The visible tests exercise SLP vectorization of intrinsic-call and vector-library mappings, not the reduced -O3 MemorySSA crash reproducer.; Some AArch64 test functions contain loads, but the modified expectations focus on call vectorization and vector shuffles rather than memory-access deletion or MemorySSA updates.
Pass or subsystem link: SLPVectorizer; intrinsic/vector-library call vectorization
Causal explanation: This candidate can alter optimized IR substantially by replacing scalar call packs with vector calls and shuffles, which could indirectly affect later optimizer pipelines. However, the retrieved evidence contains only test changes, identifies no MemorySSA maintenance path, and does not show deletion or rewiring of memory instructions. The direct evidence-backed connection to the removeFromLookups assertion is therefore weak.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Retrieved changes are test-only; no implementation hunk was provided.; Updated FileCheck expectations cover NVPTX, X86, and AArch64 SLP output.; The transformed IR uses vector intrinsics and shufflevector operations, but no build-system or API changes are visible.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The VPlan change moves creation of header PHI recipes to occur after initial scalar VPlan optimizations. The retrieved evidence is test-only, but the updated checks show loop-header induction PHIs changing from WIDEN-INDUCTION recipes to EMIT-SCALAR PHI recipes and place VPlanTransforms::createHeaderPhiRecipes after earlier plan processing.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::createHeaderPhiRecipes; VPlanTransforms::replaceSymbolicStrides; redundant_or_1; redundant_or_2; redundant_and_1; redundant_and_2; f1; reverse_unmasked_load_feeds_address
Behavioral change: Header PHI recipe creation is scheduled after initial scalar optimizations rather than before them.; VPlan test expectations now represent loop induction/header PHIs as EMIT-SCALAR PHI recipes in affected plans, instead of WIDEN-INDUCTION recipes.; The plan-print sequencing checks now expect createHeaderPhiRecipes before replaceSymbolicStrides at the updated point in the transformation sequence.
Assertion or trace link: No retrieved hunk mentions MemorySSA, removeFromLookups, memory accesses with remaining uses, or an assertion/crash.
Reproducer link: The visible tests exercise LoopVectorize/VPlan scalar simplification and loops containing stores, but do not reproduce an -O3 crash or a MemorySSA failure.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VPlanTransforms::createHeaderPhiRecipes
Causal explanation: This commit changes vectorizer plan construction and can alter the eventual loop IR and placement of scalar PHIs around memory-containing loops. That is only an indirect connection to a MemorySSA bookkeeping assertion: the retrieved evidence contains no MemorySSA updater/user change and no deletion or replacement of memory instructions. It is therefore a weak bisect candidate based on subsystem proximity to loop optimization rather than a demonstrated causal mechanism.
Causal confidence: 0.10
Build risk: Retrieved changes are test expectation updates only; no implementation hunk is available to independently verify the code path.; Tests cover VPlan textual output and scalar recipe formation for loops with conditional stores.; No dedicated MemorySSA verifier, assertion, or crash regression test is visible.

; %or = and false, %cmp folds to false, simplifying the dependent select and
; branch-on-cond to false directly.
define void @redundant_and_2(ptr %dst, i1 %c.0, i1 %c.1) {
; CHECK-LABEL: VPlan for loop in 'redundant_and_2' after VPlanTransforms::simplifyRecipes
; CHECK-NEXT:  VPlan ' for UF>=1' {
; CHECK-NEXT:  Live-in ir<3> = original trip-count
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  ir-bb<entry>:
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  vector.ph:
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): loop.header
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  loop.header:
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT-SCALAR ir<%iv> = phi [ ir<0>, vector.ph ], [ ir<%iv.next>, loop.latch ]
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT branch-on-cond ir<%c.0>
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): loop.latch, then.1
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  then.1:
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT ir<%cmp> = icmp eq ir<%iv>, ir<2>
; CHE

define void @redundant_and_2(ptr %dst, i1 %c.0, i1 %c.1) {
; CHECK-LABEL: VPlan for loop in 'redundant_and_2' after VPlanTransforms::simplifyRecipes
; CHECK-NEXT:  VPlan ' for UF>=1' {
; CHECK-NEXT:  Live-in ir<3> = original trip-count
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  ir-bb<entry>:
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  vector.ph:
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): loop.header
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  loop.header:
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT-SCALAR ir<%iv> = phi [ ir<0>, vector.ph ], [ ir<%iv.next>, loop.latch ]
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT branch-on-cond ir<%c.0>
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): loop.latch, then.1
; CHECK-EMPTY:
; CHECK-NEXT:  then.1:
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT ir<%cmp> = icmp eq ir<%iv>, ir<2>
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT ir<%or> = and ir<false>, ir<%cmp>
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT ir<%cond> = select ir<false>, ir<%c.1>, ir<false>
; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT branch-on-cond ir<false>
; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): then.2, loop.latch
;
entry:
  br label %loop.header

loop.header:
  %iv = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.latch ]
  br i1 %c.0, label %loop.latch, label %then.1

then.1:
  %cmp = icmp eq i32 %iv, 2
  %or = and i1 false, %cmp
  %cond = select i1 %or, i1 %c.1, i1 false
  br i1 %cond, label %then.2, label %loop.latch

then.2:
  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %dst, i32 %iv
  store i32 0, ptr %gep, align 4
  br label %loop.latch

loop.latch:
  %iv.next = add nuw nsw i32 %iv, 1
  %ec = icmp eq i32 %iv.next, 3
  br i1 %ec, label %exit, label %loop.header

exit:
  ret void
}

Summary: This change makes selected writable-dereferenceability queries ignore intervening frees when SimplifyCFG speculates a store and when LICM promotes loop accesses to scalars. It threads an IgnoreFree parameter through Loads.cpp dereferenceability helpers and changes the two transformation call sites to pass true, based on comments that actual dereferenceability has already been established by an existing access and the remaining query is only enforcing writability.
Changed symbols: isSafeToSpeculateStore; llvm::promoteLoopAccessesToScalars; isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointerViaAssumption; llvm::isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer; isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointer; SimplifyCFG; LICM
Behavioral change: SimplifyCFG's store-speculation safety check now calls isDereferenceablePointer with IgnoreFree=true.; LICM scalar-promotion eligibility now calls isDereferenceablePointer with IgnoreFree=true.; The underlying dereferenceability analysis propagates IgnoreFree through recursive pointer forms, including relocated pointers, bitcasts, and selects, so it can skip the willNotFreeBetween requirement when requested.; This can enable store speculation or LICM access promotion in cases previously rejected because a free could occur between pointer definition and the query context.
Reproducer link: The commit adds/adjusts SimplifyCFG speculate-store test invocation under dereferenceable-at-point semantics, but no reduced Clang -O3 MemorySSA crash reproducer is shown.

Causal explanation: The change directly alters whether LICM can promote loop memory accesses and whether SimplifyCFG can speculate stores. Those transformations modify memory instructions and are plausible indirect triggers for MemorySSA maintenance at -O3. In particular, enabling an additional LICM memory-promotion path could exercise MemorySSA bookkeeping that was previously not reached. However, no retrieved hunk references MemorySSA, removeFromLookups, memory-access deletion, or updating/removing MemorySSA uses, so there is no direct evidence that this commit violates the reported 'still has uses' invariant.

+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -disable-output  -force-vector-width=4  < %s \
+; RUN:   -vplan-print-before=simplify -vplan-print-before=printFinalVPlan \

+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -disable-output  -force-vector-width=4  < %s \
+; RUN:   -vplan-print-after=simplify -vplan-print-after=printFinalVPlan \
+; RUN:   2>&1 | FileCheck %s -DBEFORE_OR_AFTER=after --check-prefix=CHECK \
+; RUN:           --implicit-check-not "VPlan after"
+; REQUIRES: asserts
+
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] simplifyRecipes
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] simplifyBlends
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] simplifyRecipes
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] printFinalVPlan
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Final VPlan for VF={4},UF={1}' {
+
+define void @foo(ptr %ptr, i64 %n) {
+entry:
+  br label %header
+
+header:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %header ]
+  %gep = getelementptr i64, ptr %ptr, i64 %iv
+  store i64 %iv, ptr %gep
+  %iv.next = add nsw i64 %iv, 1
+  %exitcond = icmp slt i64 %iv.next, %n
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %header, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

Summary: The retrieved patch is test-only and updates AMDGPU SLPVectorizer and VectorCombine expectations for i8 vector extraction/insertion profitability. The revised expected output retains whole-vector loads and extracts selected lanes, avoids previously expected scalarized loads and redundant extract/insert reconstruction chains, and changes the expected vector construction selected for the AMDGPU arithmetic test.
Changed symbols: arith_3; extract_insert_chain_to_shuffles; test_v16i8_load_with_extracts_scalarize; extract_insert_chain
Behavioral change: The AMDGPU tests now expect VectorCombine to preserve a <16 x i8> load followed by extractelement operations instead of scalarizing selected lane loads.; The extract/insert-chain-to-shuffles test now expects an identity reconstruction of the input vector to be eliminated, producing add <16 x i8> %in, %add directly.; The SLPVectorizer AMDGPU expectations change the selected scalar lane and vector insertion/shuffle form for arith_3.; No cost-model or transformation implementation hunk is retrieved, so the underlying profitability rule change is not available.
Pass or subsystem link: AMDGPU SLPVectorizer; AMDGPU VectorCombine
Causal explanation: The changed tests exercise vector transformations around loads, stores, extracts, inserts, and shuffles, which can alter IR containing memory operations. Nevertheless, the evidence is restricted to AMDGPU test expectations; it contains no MemorySSA API or implementation change, no MemorySSA update/removal operation, and no match to the reported removeFromLookups assertion. The connection to the generic -O3 MemorySSA crash is therefore indirect and weak.
Causal confidence: 0.03
Build risk: All retrieved hunks are test expectation changes under AMDGPU-specific SLPVectorizer and VectorCombine tests.; The changed tests cover vector load/store and extract/insert IR patterns.; No implementation, build-system, or MemorySSA compilation changes are visible in the retrieved evidence.

top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] Fold X == Identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) (#202748)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: InstructionSimplify's simplifyWithOpsReplaced now recognizes MinMaxIntrinsic calls whose replaced operands include the intrinsic identity value. It returns the other operand in that case, subject to preserving poison semantics: poison-generating annotations prevent the fold unless the caller permits dropping flags, in which case the intrinsic is recorded in DropFlags. The accompanying InstCombine tests cover unsigned/signed min/max identity cases and a negative case with the wrong selected bound.
Changed symbols: simplifyWithOpsReplaced; MinMaxIntrinsic::getIdentity; select_signed_max_smin; select_npos_umin; select_not_npos_umin; select_npos_umin_commuted; select_npos_wrong_bound_negative; select_npos_umin_drop_range
Behavioral change: When operand replacement makes either operand of a MinMaxIntrinsic equal to that min/max operation's identity, simplifyWithOpsReplaced returns the other operand.; For min/max intrinsics with poison-generating annotations, the simplification is rejected unless DropFlags is available; when allowed, the intrinsic is added to DropFlags before returning the simplified value.; The tests expect select patterns guarding min/max operations at their identity bounds to fold to the min/max result, while retaining a non-folding case whose selected replacement value is not the corresponding bound.
Reproducer link: The change affects scalar simplification/InstCombine behavior that can run in an -O3 pipeline, but the retrieved tests are pure integer min/max/select patterns and do not reproduce a crash.
Pass or subsystem link: InstructionSimplify; InstCombine; scalar optimizer
Causal explanation: This commit directly changes scalar simplification used by InstCombine, a subsystem identified as potentially relevant to the -O3 optimizer failure. Its fold can cause an instruction to be replaced and later removed, which is generally the kind of IR mutation that must be correctly reflected in analyses. However, MinMaxIntrinsic is a pure integer operation in the shown code, and the patch neither references MemorySSA nor manipulates memory accesses, MemoryAccess users, or removeFromLookups. There is no direct evidence that this fold reaches the reported MemorySSA assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.12
Build risk: The patch includes a production implementation change in llvm/lib/Analysis/InstructionSimplify.cpp.; It adds targeted InstCombine regression tests for signed and unsigned min/max identity folds.; The implementation explicitly guards poison-generating annotations through DropFlags, indicating semantic sensitivity around instruction replacement and flag dropping.; No MemorySSA-specific test or implementation coverage is present in the retrieved hunks.

top_candidates.subject: [GVN][NFC] Use InsertPt in MaterializeAdjustedValue (#204335)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: GVN changes AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue so that a rematerialized select is inserted at the supplied insertion point rather than at the original select instruction's iterator. The associated GVN/PRE tests update expected select placement and debug-location ordering. Although labeled NFC, this changes where GVN materializes an IR instruction during load/select PRE.
Changed symbols: llvm::gvn::AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; AvailableValueInBlock::MaterializeAdjustedValue; SelectInst::Create; test_pointer_phi_select_simp_1; test_pointer_phi_select_same_object; test_pointer_phi_select_same_object_invoke_in_chain; test
Behavioral change: When materializing an adjusted select value, GVN now uses InsertPt->getIterator() instead of Sel->getIterator().; The newly materialized SelectInst is therefore placed relative to the requested insertion point, rather than relative to the source SelectInst.; Tests show corresponding ordering changes for generated selects and their debug locations.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses
Reproducer link: The changed code is used by GVN/PRE transformations involving loads, pointer selects, PHIs, loops, and invokes, which are optimizer patterns potentially present in an -O3 testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; GVN PRE; Scalar optimizer; MemorySSA-adjacent optimization
Causal explanation: This is a plausible but indirect candidate. GVN rematerializes IR around loads and selects, and instruction placement can affect subsequent optimization and analysis-update behavior. However, the changed instruction is a non-memory SelectInst, and the retrieved implementation contains no MemorySSA construction, update, removal, or use-rewriting operation. The evidence therefore does not directly connect this placement correction to removing a MemoryAccess that still has uses.
Causal confidence: 0.22
Build risk: Implementation change in Scalar/GVN despite the NFC label.; Multiple GVN and PRE output checks change, including debug-location ordering and select placement.; No retrieved test invocation exercises this revision under gvn<memoryssa>.

Summary: This is a test-regeneration commit for GVN that adds separate test runs and check prefixes for ordinary memory-dependence GVN and GVN configured with MemorySSA, gvn<memoryssa>. The regenerated checks capture output differences between those modes, including a loop/load-through-select case where the MemorySSA mode retains an exit-block load rather than the ordinary-mode materialized value/select result. No GVN or MemorySSA implementation code is changed in the retrieved hunks.
Changed symbols: gvn; gvn<memoryssa>; test_pointer_phi_select_load_may_not_execute_1; test_pointer_phi_select_simp_1; test_pointer_phi_select_same_object; test

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

Summary: The retrieved evidence is test-only, but it expands and updates SimpleLoopUnswitch coverage for generalized trivial unswitching. New tests exercise loop-invariant guard branches whose latch-directed edge is rewired into an exit-like edge, including nested loops containing loads and stores, and update phase-ordering expectations to reflect a different unswitched CFG.
Changed symbols: SimpleLoopUnswitch; unswitchTrivialBranch; perfect_nest_guard; _Z7computeRSt6vectorIiSaIiEEy; _Z11hotFunctionbiiPiS_S_
Behavioral change: Retrieved tests expect trivial unswitching of a loop-invariant guard in a perfect loop nest when one arm originally targets the outer-loop latch.; The new guard test documents that the latch arm is rewritten to the outer-loop exit so standard trivial-unswitch logic can hoist the invariant branch.; Phase-ordering checks change expected CFG layout, loop metadata references, preheaders, and placement of an inner load/store loop after unswitching.; The new cold-function test distinguishes non-trivial loop unswitching, which duplicates a loop body and remains suppressed for optsize/minsize functions, from the latch-bypass trivial form.

Pass or subsystem link: SimpleLoopUnswitch; Loop pass manager with MemorySSA support via loop-mssa; PhaseOrdering

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {

top_candidates.subject: [GVN][NFC] Use InsertPt in MaterializeAdjustedValue (#204335)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: GVN changes AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue so that a rematerialized select is inserted at the caller-provided InsertPt rather than at the original select instruction's iterator. The accompanying GVN/PRE test updates reflect the resulting instruction-order and debug-location ordering changes.
Changed symbols: llvm::gvn::AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; AvailableValueInBlock::MaterializeAdjustedValue; test_pointer_phi_select_simp_1; test_pointer_phi_select_same_object
Behavioral change: SelectInst::Create now uses InsertPt->getIterator() instead of Sel->getIterator().; GVN/PRE rematerialized selects are placed at the requested insertion point, rather than being anchored beside the source select.; The change can reorder non-memory select instructions relative to surrounding transformed loads and debug locations.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses
Reproducer link: The affected code is GVN load/select materialization and PRE-style load-through-select transformation, which is in the optimizer area implicated by the -O3 crash.; No retrieved hunk contains the reported assertion, a MemorySSA removal call, or the reduced C reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; Scalar optimizer; GVN PRE/load-through-select transformations
Causal explanation: This is a real GVN transformation-order change in a path that materializes values while optimizing loads, so it could indirectly alter the instruction/update sequence seen by MemorySSA-enabled GVN. However, the modified instruction is a select rather than a memory access, and no retrieved implementation hunk updates MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, or access-use bookkeeping. The evidence therefore supports only an indirect and limited connection to the removeFromLookups assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.20
Build risk: Changes production code in llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/GVN.cpp.; Updates several GVN/PRE FileCheck expectations, indicating intentional output-order changes.; No direct MemorySSA implementation or invariant test is changed in the retrieved hunks.
