top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This IRBuilder intrinsic-creation refactor adapts scalar and utility clients to intrinsic constant folding and possible non-CallInst results. LoopIdiomRecognize and ScalarEvolutionExpander change local results from CallInst* to Value* where folding may occur; LoopIdiomRecognize explicitly uses CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding for the strided-store path; and intrinsic debug-location and flag propagation are moved into IRBuilder creation APIs. The retrieved LoopIdiomRecognize pass context shows that this pass receives AR.MSSA and preserves MemorySSAAnalysis after successful loop transformations.
Changed symbols: LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStridedStore; createPopcntIntrinsic; createFFSIntrinsic; LoopIdiomRecognize::recognizeShiftUntilZero; LoopIdiomRecognize::recognizeShiftUntilBitTest; LibCallSimplifier::replacePowWithExp; SCEVExpander::generateOverflowCheck; LoopIdiomRecognizePass::run
Behavioral change: Intrinsic construction callers are adapted from assuming a CallInst result to accepting a Value result where intrinsic creation may fold.; LoopIdiomRecognize::processLoopStridedStore switches to CreateIntrinsicWithoutFolding, explicitly retaining an intrinsic instruction rather than permitting folding in that path.; createPopcntIntrinsic and createFFSIntrinsic set the builder's current debug location before creation rather than assigning it after creating a CallInst.; replacePowWithExp supplies an IRBuilder callback to copy IR flags onto a newly created exp10 intrinsic call.
Assertion or trace link: The retrieved context explicitly references MemorySSAAnalysis and AR.MSSA.; No direct MemorySSA::removeFromLookups or "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses" diagnostic appears in the shown hunks.
Reproducer link: The change affects loop idiom recognition and scalar-evolution expansion, both optimizer transformations that can run under optimized compilation, but no direct mapping to the reduced C testcase is shown.

Changing whether intrinsic creation materializes an instruction or folds to a non-instruction can alter the transform's instruction graph and deletion/replacement behavior, precisely where MemorySSA bookkeeping must remain consistent. The explicit no-folding change in processLoopStridedStore further shows sensitivity to preserving an actual instruction in a loop transformation. steps.subject: [SimplifyCFG] Use context instruction in foldBranchToCommonDest() (#203516)

evidence: SimplifyCFG changes whether dereferenceable loads are speculated while performing CFG rewrites, directly changing memory instruction placement.
It is in Transforms/Utils and affects scalar optimizer memory operations, but the visible caller passes a null MSSA updater and no access-removal code is shown.
features: cfg-rewrite, load-speculation, memory-access-placement, memoryssa-indirect, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/include/llvm/Transforms
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Updates SimplifyCFG's foldBranchToCommonDest speculation safety check to query dereferenceability in the context where a speculated instruction will be inserted. The transformation now passes AssumptionCache into foldBranchToCommonDest and uses the sole predecessor's terminator as context when there is exactly one predecessor, avoiding speculation decisions based on assumptions that are not valid at the insertion point.
Changed symbols: llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest; SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch; isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute; AssumptionCache; load_derefable; load_derefable_assume; load_derefable_assume_var
Behavioral change: Adds an AssumptionCache parameter to foldBranchToCommonDest.; Computes a context instruction from the unique predecessor terminator when speculated instructions will be inserted in that predecessor.; Calls isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute with the insertion context and assumption cache rather than using a context-free query.; Allows or suppresses folding/speculation of dereferenceable loads according to whether the relevant assume is valid at the actual insertion point.
Assertion or trace link: No direct MemorySSA::removeFromLookups or "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses" assertion appears in the retrieved hunks.; The changed call site explicitly invokes foldBranchToCommonDest with MSSAU set to nullptr.
Reproducer link: The new tests cover branch folding that moves dereferenceable loads into a predecessor, including parameter attributes, constant assume-bundle sizes, variable assume-bundle sizes, and multi-predecessor cases.; These are optimizer CFG and load-speculation patterns that can affect the set and placement of memory instructions, but no -O3 crash reproducer is shown.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; Transforms/Utils; AssumptionCache; speculative load safety
Causal explanation: This is a stronger candidate than a purely analysis-only change because it changes whether SimplifyCFG creates or moves load instructions while rewriting CFG edges. Those changes can affect later MemorySSA construction or updates. However, the retrieved changed simplifyCondBranch call does not supply a MemorySSA updater, and no direct MemorySSA mutation or removal path is visible, so the evidence supports only an indirect causal route.

Summary: Corrects default operand values used by llvm::getKnowledgeFromBundle for assume bundles: alignment retains a default of 1, while dereferenceable and dereferenceable_or_null use a default of 0. The accompanying SimplifyCFG tests distinguish a known dereferenceable size of 1, which permits load speculation, from an unknown size, which does not.
Changed symbols: llvm::getKnowledgeFromBundle; GetArgOr; align_deref_size_1; align_deref_size_unknown
Behavioral change: Replaces the unconditional missing-operand default of 1 with an attribute-specific default.; Treats missing dereferenceable and dereferenceable_or_null bundle size operands as 0 rather than 1.; Prevents an unknown dereferenceable size from being interpreted as sufficient proof that a one-byte load may be speculated.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The implementation change in GVN changes where `AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue` inserts a rematerialized `select`: instead of inserting relative to the original source select (`Sel->getIterator()`), it inserts relative to the requested materialization point (`InsertPt->getIterator()`). The accompanying GVN/PRE tests update expected select ordering and debug-location association, consistent with the rematerialized select moving to the requested insertion position.
Changed symbols: AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; test_pointer_phi_select_simp_1; test_pointer_phi_select_same_object; test; loadtree
Behavioral change: A `SelectInst` rematerialized by `AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue` is now inserted immediately before the supplied `InsertPt` rather than before the original source select.; GVN/PRE expected IR changes place synthesized selects at a different location in affected blocks.; The changed placement also changes which debug locations are attached to the reordered select instructions in `debugloc-load-select.ll`.
Reproducer link: The visible tests cover GVN/PRE load-through-select transformations, but no `-O3` reduced-C crash or MemorySSA assertion is present.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; GVN PRE; load-through-select materialization
Causal explanation: This commit changes instruction placement during a scalar optimization that materializes values derived from loads. Incorrect placement can affect dominance, ordering, and the resulting IR consumed by later optimizer passes. Nevertheless, the generated instruction is a `select`, not a memory access, and the retrieved implementation hunk contains no MemorySSA update or removal operation. The tests demonstrate ordering and debug-location changes, not a MemorySSA access-use invariant failure, so the connection to `MemorySSA::removeFromLookups` remains indirect.

Build risk: The implementation change is a localized insertion-point substitution in GVN.; Multiple GVN/PRE tests update expected instruction order, indicating intentional IR-ordering changes that could expose dominance or ordering regressions.; Debug-location expectations also change, providing test coverage for observable placement effects.

top_candidates.subject: [Loads][LAA] Properly handle multiple deref assumptions (#204083)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved hunks add LoopVectorize regression coverage for a loop with two dereferenceability assumptions on the same pointer: one constant-size and one `%n`-sized. The test asserts that the extra constant assumption does not prevent vectorization, and existing check references are renumbered after the inserted test. No LAA, LoopVectorize, or MemorySSA implementation hunk is included in the retrieved material.
Changed symbols: deref_assumption_in_preheader_non_constant_trip_count_access_i8_extra_constant_assume; deref_assumption_in_preheader_non_constant_trip_count_access_i32; deref_assumption_in_preheader_non_constant_trip_count_access_i32_al; deref_assumption_loop_access_start_variable; deref_assumption_loop_access_start_variable_unknown_range
Behavioral change: A new test requires LoopVectorize to continue vectorizing when `%a` has both a constant `dereferenceable` assumption and a variable-size `dereferenceable` assumption.; The expected vectorized loop performs vector loads from `%a` and `%b`, selects values, and vector-stores to `%c`, with scalar remainder handling.; The other visible changes are FileCheck loop-metadata variable renumberings caused by inserting the new test.
Reproducer link: LoopVectorize test using `llvm.assume` dereferenceability bundles and vector loads/stores; no pr204589 crash, `MemorySSA::removeFromLookups`, or 'still has uses' diagnostic is present.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; Loop Access Analysis; assumption-derived dereferenceability
Causal explanation: The test exercises memory-access-heavy loop vectorization, which is generally adjacent to optimizer memory bookkeeping. Nevertheless, the retrieved evidence concerns dereferenceability inference and expected vectorization, not MemorySSA access deletion or use-list maintenance. With no implementation hunk showing how LAA or LoopVectorize updates MemorySSA, there is no evidence-backed causal path to the reported remove-from-lookups assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.02
Build risk: Retrieved hunks add and update LLVM IR/FileCheck tests only.; The new regression test may expose changes in LoopVectorize or LAA assumption handling.; Because implementation hunks were not retrieved, production build and runtime risk cannot be established from this evidence.

+; Wave64 shuffle patterns. The index must be the full wave64 thread ID,

+; lane & 0x1F and is not a wave-wide permutation.

+declare i32 @llvm.amdgcn.mbcnt.lo(i32, i32)
+declare i32 @llvm.amdgcn.mbcnt.hi(i32, i32)
+declare i32 @llvm.amdgcn.wave.shuffle.i32(i32, i32)
+

+; GFX11-W64-LABEL: @test_identity_w64(

+  %lo = call i32 @llvm.amdgcn.mbcnt.lo(i32 -1, i32 0)
+  %lane = call i32 @llvm.amdgcn.mbcnt.hi(i32 -1, i32 %lo)
+  %result = call i32 @llvm.amdgcn.wave.shuffle.i32(i32 %val, i32 %lane)
+  ret i32 %result
+}
+
+; Quad perm: lane ^ 1 swaps adjacent pairs.
+define i32 @test_quad_perm_xor1_w64(i32 %val) {
+; GFX11-W64-LABEL: @test_quad_perm_xor1_w64(

+; GFX9-NEXT:    ret i32 [[RESULT]]

+  %lane = call i32 @llvm.amdgcn.mbcnt.hi(i32 -1, i32 %lo)

evidence: Changes MLIR XeGPU-to-XeVM load type conversion for narrow floating-point storage representations.

features: llvm-dialect-load-types, mlir-xegpu-lowering, path:mlir/lib/Conversion/XeGPUToXeVM, path:mlir/test/Conversion/XeGPUToXeVM, term:fix, term:gettypeconverter
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Fixes XeGPU load_matrix lowering for element types without a direct LLVM representation by deriving the LLVM load result type from the conversion type converter rather than directly using the original vector element type. This preserves scalarization of one-element vectors while loading an integer storage representation, such as i8 for f8E8M0FNU, followed by the existing materialization/bitcast back to the source element type.
Changed symbols: LoadStoreMatrixToXeVMPattern; LLVM::LoadOp; getTypeConverter; load_matrix_f8e8m0_scalar; load_matrix_f8e8m0_vector
Behavioral change: XeGPU load_matrix lowering now uses convertType(op.getResult().getType()) as the LLVM load type.; Non-native LLVM element types such as f8E8M0FNU are loaded through same-width integer storage types rather than being used directly as illegal LLVM load result types.; Single-element vectors continue to lower to scalar loads because the type converter collapses them to scalar types.; New conversion tests check scalar i8 loads plus arith.bitcast and vector i8 loads plus vector.bitcast for f8E8M0FNU.

selected_hunks.patch:
@@ -309,0 +310,24 @@ gpu.module @test_kernel [#xevm.target<chip = "pvc">] {
+  // f8E8M0FNU has no native LLVM representation. The load must use the integer
+  // storage type from the XeVM type converter (i8) and then materialize back
+  // to f8E8M0FNU, rather than emitting an illegal llvm.load of f8E8M0FNU.
+  //CHECK-LABEL: load_matrix_f8e8m0_scalar
+  gpu.func @load_matrix_f8e8m0_scalar(%arg0: memref<1024xi8, 3>) -> vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU> {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %0 = xegpu.create_mem_desc %arg0 : memref<1024xi8, 3> -> !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>
+    %tid_x = gpu.thread_id x
+    //CHECK: %[[LOADED:.*]] = llvm.load %{{.*}} : !llvm.ptr<3> -> i8
+    //CHECK: %[[BCAST:.*]] = arith.bitcast %[[LOADED]] : i8 to f8E8M0FNU
+    //CHECK: vector.broadcast %[[BCAST]] : f8E8M0FNU to vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU>
+    %1 = xegpu.load_matrix %0[%c0, %tid_x]: !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>, index, index -> vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU>
+    gpu.return %1 : vector<1x1xf8E8M0FNU>
+  }
+
+  //CHECK-LABEL: load_matrix_f8e8m0_vector
+  gpu.func @load_matrix_f8e8m0_vector(%arg0: memref<1024xi8, 3>) -> vector<8xf8E8M0FNU> {
+    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
+    %0 = xegpu.create_mem_desc %arg0 : memref<1024xi8, 3> -> !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>
+    //CHECK: %[[LOADEDV:.*]] = llvm.load %{{.*}} : !llvm.ptr<3> -> vector<8xi8>
+    //CHECK: vector.bitcast %[[LOADEDV]] : vector<8xi8> to vector<8xf8E8M0FNU>
+    %1 = xegpu.load_matrix %0[%c0, %c0]: !xegpu.mem_desc<32x32xf8E8M0FNU>, index, index -> vector<8xf8E8M0FNU>
+    gpu.return %1 : vector<8xf8E8M0FNU>
+  }

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

diff --git a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
index d09def0afdb7..6e56dfd783d1 100644
--- a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
+++ b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
@@ -494,0 +495,25 @@ endfunction()
+# PluginManager discovers dynamic script interpreter plugins at runtime by
+# scanning the directory that holds liblldb, so a plugin is loaded only when it
+# sits beside it. A framework build moves liblldb into the bundle, so the plugin
+# must move with it and carry an rpath that reaches liblldb from its new
+# location.
+function(lldb_add_scriptinterpreter_plugin_to_framework name)
+  if(NOT LLDB_BUILD_FRAMEWORK)
+    return()
+  endif()
+  set_property(TARGET ${name} APPEND PROPERTY
+    INSTALL_RPATH "@loader_path/../../..")
+  # Copy under the unversioned name: PluginManager derives a plugin's
+  # initializer symbol from it. A versioned copy would load but never
+  # initialize.
+  set(plugin_in_framework
+    "${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_ABSOLUTE_BUILD_DIR}/LLDB.framework/Versions/${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_VERSION}/$<TARGET_LINKER_FILE_NAME:${name}>")
+  add_custom_command(TARGET ${name} POST_BUILD VERBATIM
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy "$<TARGET_FILE:${name}>" "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Copy ${name} into LLDB.framework")
+  add_custom_target(${name}-framework-cleanup
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E remove "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Removing ${name} from LLDB.framework")
+  add_dependencies(lldb-framework-cleanup ${name}-framework-cleanup)
+endfunction()

# Returns TRUE in `out_var` if any of `libs` is `liblldb` or already carries
# the LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB property.
function(_lldb_links_liblldb_check out_var libs)
  set(${out_var} FALSE PARENT_SCOPE)
  foreach(lib ${libs})
    if("${lib}" STREQUAL "liblldb")
      set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
      return()
    endif()
    if(TARGET "${lib}")
      get_target_property(_p "${lib}" LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB)
      if(_p)
        set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
        return()
      endif()
    endif()
  endforeach()
endfunction()

function(_lldb_propagate_links_liblldb name libs)
  _lldb_links_liblldb_check(_links_liblldb "${libs}")
  set_target_properties(${name} PROPERTIES LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB ${_links_liblldb})
endfunction()

function(lldb_record_dynamic_script_interpreter_exports target)
  set(symbol_file
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}.undefined.symbols")

  # llvm-nm is registered as a CMake target after the LLDB subdirectory is
  # processed, so a forward target reference is required. LLVM_NM, when set,
  # points to a prebuilt host tool for cross-compiled builds.
  if(LLVM_NM)
    set(nm_exe "${LLVM_NM}")
    set(nm_dep)
  else()
    set(nm_exe "$<TARGET_FILE:llvm-nm>")
    set(nm_dep llvm-nm)
  endif()

  set(extra_args)
  if(APPLE)
    list(APPEND extra_args --mach-o)
  endif()

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT ${symbol_file}
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"
      ${LLDB_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/extract-dynamic-script-interpreter-exports.py
      --nm ${nm_exe}
      ${extra_args}
      -o ${symbol_file}
      $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${target}>
    DEPENDS
      ${LLDB_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/extract-dynamic-script-interpreter-exports.py
      $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${target}>
      ${nm_dep}
    COMMAND_EXPAND_LISTS
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "Extracting LLDB symbols required by ${target}"
  )

  add_custom_target(${target}-exports DEPENDS ${symbol_file})
  set_target_properties(${target}-exports PROPERTIES FOLDER "LLDB/API")

  set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PR

lldb_add_scriptinterpreter_plugin_to_framework(lldbPluginScriptInterpreterPython)

  # Static variant linked directly by unit tests. Separate compilation is
  # required so llvm::Error RTTI (ErrorInfoBase::ID) has a single address
  # shared between the test binary and the plugin code.
  add_lldb_library(lldbStaticScriptInterpreterPython
    ${python_plugin_sources}
    LINK_COMPONENTS
      Support
    LINK_LIBS
      lldbBreakpoint
      lldbCore
      lldbDataFormatters
      lldbHost
      lldbInterpreter
      lldbTarget
      lldbValueObject
      ${Python3_LIBRARIES}
      ${LLDB_LIBEDIT_LIBS}
  )
  target_include_directories(lldbStaticScriptInterpreterPython
    PUBLIC ${Python3_INCLUDE_DIRS})
  target_link_directories(lldbStaticScriptInterpreterPython
    PUBLIC ${PYTHON_SABI_LIBRARY_DIRS})
else()
  # On Windows with the limited API, the Python import library is selected via
  # #pragma comment(lib, ...) in pyconfig.h based on Py_LIMITED_API.
  # On all other platforms, always link Python3_LIBRARIES explicitly.
  if (NOT (WIN32 AND LLDB_ENABLE_PYTHON_LIMITED_API))
    set(python_link_libs ${Python3_LIBRARIES})
  endif()
  add_lldb_library(lldbPluginScriptInterpreterPython PLUGIN
    ${python_plugin_sources}
    LINK_COMPONENTS
      Support
    LINK_LIBS
      lldbBreakpoint
      lldbCore
      lldbDataFormatters
      lldbHost
      lldbInterpreter
      lldbTarget
      lldbValueObject
      ${python_link_libs}
      ${LLDB_LIBEDIT_LIBS}
  )
  target_link_directories(lldbPluginScriptInterpreterPython PUBLIC ${PYTHON_SABI_LIBRARY_DIRS})
endif()

target_include_directories(lldbPluginScriptInterpreterPython
  PUBLIC ${Python3_INCLUDE_DIRS})

+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;

+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).

+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:

+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]

+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;

+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17

+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]

+  br label %loop.latch

+if.else:

+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires

+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.

+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)

+;;     }

+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
